paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 (%) and the number of child nodes, which represents tree width, for two large language models: GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis, labeled "Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)", is linearly scaled from 1 to 7, with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy@1 (%)", is linearly scaled from 15 to 35, with tick marks at 5-unit intervals. The blue line with circle markers represents GPT-4o, starting at 24.4% accuracy at a tree width of 1, rising to a peak of 34.4% at a tree width of 5, and then declining to 31.1% at a tree width of 7. The light purple line with cross markers represents Claude-3.5-Sonnet, starting at 26.7% accuracy at a tree width of 1, rising to 27.8% at a tree width of 3, then declining to 24.4% at a tree width of 5, and further declining to 20.0% at a tree width of 7. Both lines exhibit an inverted U-shaped trend, with performance increasing to a peak and then decreasing as tree width increases.
